title: Abomasum, Lower Digestive Tract, and Accessory Organs
text:
Abomasum "true stomach"
○ True, glandular stomach
○ Similar function to monogastric stomach that secretes gastric juices which aid in digestion.

Abomasum of a cow

Lower digestive tract
○ Small intestine - is where proteins, fats, and carbohydrates that leave the abomasum are absorbed.
○ Large intestine - is where water primarily absorbed.

Accessory organs
○ Liver - is a major site for metabolism of nutrients and also produces bile which is stored in the gall bladder.
○ Pancreas - secretes buffers and enzymes into the small intestine.

facts: The abomasum is known as the "true stomach".
The abomasum is a true, glandular stomach.
The abomasum has a similar function to a monogastric stomach, secreting gastric juices that aid in digestion.
The lower digestive tract includes the small intestine and large intestine.
The small intestine is where proteins, fats, and carbohydrates that leave the abomasum are absorbed.
The large intestine is where water is primarily absorbed.
Accessory organs of the digestive system include the liver and pancreas.
The liver is a major site for nutrient metabolism.
The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder.
The pancreas secretes buffers and enzymes into the small intestine.
